description: Applies to repositories that publish container images to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR). It extends general.json and the applicable public/private distribution profile without replacing their validation or publication boundaries.

dos: Every repository that publishes an image to GHCR must apply ghcr-published.json in addition to general.json and its applicable public or private distribution profile.
GHCR publication is separate from general validation, npm publication, and deployment execution.
donts: Do not treat ghcr-published.json as permission to publish, deploy, or alter a live registry.

dos: After the seven general AGENTS.md headings, add a ## GHCR publication section. Document image identity, visibility, publication workflow and required validation, provenance/signing mechanism, registry credential boundary, exact digest verification, and deployment-consumer boundary. Document release gates and the Operations handoff; do not treat this profile or its documentation as permission to publish.
donts: Do not leave GHCR publication ownership, image identity, or secret-handling boundaries undocumented in AGENTS.md.

dos: Each repository must publish exactly one image name, ghcr.io/eliware/<repository-name>. Multiple tags, including a mutable latest alias, may refer to that same image name. The image is built from the repository-root Dockerfile and repository-root build context.
The repository name in the GHCR image must match the unscoped package.json.name.
donts: Do not publish under an unapproved registry owner, repository name, or image mapping.

dos: GHCR repositories must contain exactly one publication workflow at .github/workflows/publish.yml in addition to .github/workflows/ci.yml; no other GitHub Actions workflow files are allowed. If npm publication is also applied, both publication profiles use this single publish.yml file.

GHCR publication workflows must use the GitHub Actions glob `v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*` as a candidate filter, then enforce the exact `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` numeric form and verify it matches the approved package version before pushing. These publication requirements are checked statically on every validation run, including ordinary branch runs; the release tag guard is additionally compared to the current ref during tag-triggered runs. Static validation checks workflow declarations only and cannot prove GitHub environment protection or reviewer settings; verify those settings in GitHub before each authorized release. Require Eli's explicit authorization routed through the Operations release handoff. The README must document the image name, pull command, supported tags, and deployment boundary.
donts: Do not use broad tag filters that start publication workflows for prerelease or non-version tags, publish from branches, pull requests, manual validation dispatches, unversioned tags, or an inferred release version.

dos: The GHCR publication workflow must remain separate from the general validation workflow and its publication job must depend on a successful Ubuntu validation job using npm ci followed by npm test.
A repository that also publishes npm must keep npm publication separate while reusing the inherited validation result and exact release identity.
donts: Do not place GHCR credentials or GHCR publication steps in validation-only CI, Knit, or npm publication validation.

dos: A GHCR-only publication job must grant exactly contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write, attestations: write, and artifact-metadata: write. When npm-published is also applied, the publication job must grant the exact union of the permissions required by both profiles. The workflow-level permission map must be exactly contents: read; publication permissions belong only on the publication job.
donts: Do not commit, print, persist, or expose registry credentials, and do not grant broader workflow permissions than the publication requires.

dos: Every GHCR publication must generate a signed GitHub artifact attestation using actions/attest@v4 after the image push, with id-token: write, attestations: write, artifact-metadata: write, contents: read, and packages: write permissions as required by the attestation workflow.

The attestation must use the fully qualified image name without a tag and the pushed image digest as subject-digest, set push-to-registry: true, and record the attestation result with the release handoff.
donts: Do not treat provenance or signing as optional project hardening, use a tag instead of the immutable digest as the attestation subject, or publish an image without its signed attestation.

dos: The project owner must own the Dockerfile or equivalent build definition, build context, and supported-architecture declaration; DevOps executes the approved build and publication.
Single-architecture builds are the baseline; multi-architecture publication requires project-specific declaration and approval before implementation.
donts: Do not let a publication operator silently change the build context, Dockerfile, or supported architectures.

dos: The exact version tag and recorded sha256 digest together identify the published image for release and deployment.
latest may be published only as a documented mutable convenience alias and must never be the release or deployment identity.
donts: Do not deploy, hand off, or identify a release solely by latest or another mutable tag.

dos: The publication workflow must expose the pushed image digest, verify that the exact version tag resolves to that digest, and verify that the image and signed attestation are readable according to the repository visibility before reporting publication success.

In the GHCR publication job, the final image push's required digest and attestation verification chain must end at the last job step so job success proves verification completed. This ordering rule does not apply to the general CI workflow.

Every required verification stage must resolve to an actual workflow step before ordering is evaluated; a missing attestation, digest verification, inspection, or handoff stage always fails validation.
donts: Do not report GHCR publication success without digest and attestation verification.

dos: After publication, use a separate Operations release handoff and a separate GitOps deployment handoff for any rollout; publication alone must not deploy the image.
donts: Do not make GHCR publication automatically mutate GitOps desired state or live Kubernetes state.

dos: Before pushing a GHCR image, the publication job must verify that npm package.json's exact version matches the version without the v prefix in GITHUB_REF_NAME, then target the protected ghcr-publish GitHub environment configured with Eli as a required reviewer through the Operations release handoff.
donts: Do not treat tag-shaped text, a semver comment, or an unprotected environment as release-version verification or Eli's publication authorization.
